sentences.text: Third place stung less once he saw the winner's manten-stone ridge line up perfectly with its own reflection. One judge crouched at eye level with the aquarium for a full minute, saying nothing, pencil hovering. Records indicate the corydoras deposited eggs on the glass within six hours of the cool-water change. Eggs stuck to the heater cord again, which means scraping and praying half survive the move. Would the guppy line hold its blue if I stopped pulling the fan-tailed males? He logs GH and KH in a spiral notebook, one column per shelf, dated in pencil. By noon the convention hall smelled of wet soil and glue, and every competitor was pretending not to study the neighboring entries. By June the bottom shelf held four hundred fry and I had exactly zero free time. Did you see how he angled that seiryu stone, or was I imagining the forty-five-degree tilt? Selling thirty juveniles a month barely covers the electric bill for all these heaters.
